title: Cycle slot staking and role-shadowing protocol for fair capacity allocation
creator: Marisol Diaz
description:
Problem: Current cycle slot allocation tilts toward initiatives that request large contiguous time blocks early in planning; this causes specialist bottlenecks mid-cycle and repeated scope cuts. We need a lightweight, transparent protocol to surface tradeoffs and preserve fairness across initiatives while giving teams options to secure critical slots.

Proposal summary: Introduce a two-part workflow: (1) a lightweight 'slot staking' mechanic where initiative leads stake time-credit tokens (non-financial points representing specialist commitment) to claim priority for specific cycle slots, and (2) a 'role-shadowing' contingency window where teams accept a 10% planned shadow capacity commitment from adjacent cycles to cover specialist outages. The mechanism is supported by a cycle-simulator that models staffing shocks and predicts the risk of mid-cycle scope cuts.

Why this is different: existing playbooks focus on buffers or tranche reserves. Slot staking makes claims visible and creates a small, reversible commitment that reduces surprise mid-cycle reallocation. Role-shadowing codifies temporary cross-team coverage expectations to reduce single-person critical-path outages.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator accuracy: predicted vs actual specialist shortfall error <= 15% after two pilot cycles
Allocation variance: standard deviation of weekly assigned specialist hours across initiatives decreases by >= 12% compared to baseline cycle
Scope-stability: number of mid-cycle scope cuts attributed to specialist availability reduces by >= 30% in pilot teams
Adoption: at least 6 initiatives use slot staking during pilot and consent to role-shadowing agreements
Psychological safety check: post-cycle survey median rating for perceived fairness >= 3.8/5 among participating PMs
proposal:
Step 1: Pilot slot-staking in two product areas (Console and Dedicated). Each initiative is allocated 10 stake tokens for the cycle planning window. Teams may spend 1-5 tokens on slots (morning/afternoon week blocks) to indicate criticality; tokens are refunded if engineer-level coverage is committed in the staffing sheet. Step 2: Implement role-shadowing slots where adjacent squads commit to a 1.5 day/week total shadow capacity for the first 4 weeks of the cycle. Step 3: Run the cycle-simulator with three staffing-shock scenarios (one sick-leave cluster, one hiring delay, one urgent outage) and generate a risk score for each initiative. Step 4: Retrospective and OKR tie-in: feed outcomes into the cycle-planner dashboard and create an "allocation fairness" metric for leadership reviews.

Operational notes: slot staking is non-monetary and advisory; it should not change payroll or HR policy. Role-shadowing is time-limited and documented in the staffing sheet. The simulator is a Monte Carlo model with historical absence and throughput distributions derived from last 12 cycles.
decisions: Pilot limited to two product areas to minimize cross-team friction
Stake tokens per initiative fixed at 10 for pilot to simplify calibration
Role-shadowing capped at 10% of a squad's sprint capacity and expires after week 4 unless extended by mutual agreement
Simulator scenarios chosen to reflect the three highest-frequency disruption modes from incident history
